duress.title: Duress password
duress.description: A second password that, when entered at unlock, silently wipes the local vault and opens an empty decoy. For coercion scenarios.
duress.hint: ⚠ Must differ from your master password. Stored as a SHA-256 hash only. Cloud backups are not wiped — remove those separately for full protection.
duress.setToastBody: Entering it will wipe the local vault and show a decoy.

extension.title: Browser extension
extension.description: Push a minimal snapshot (title, URL, username, password, TOTP) to the companion Chrome extension for autofill. The extension holds it in memory only and auto-clears after 5 minutes idle.
extension.findId: Find the ID at chrome://extensions (Developer mode).
extension.unavailable: Not available here — the extension bridge needs SecureVault open as a page in Chrome or Edge. It doesn't work from the desktop app.
extension.failedBody: Is the extension installed and the ID correct?

sync.title: WebDAV backup
sync.description: Push or pull the encrypted vault to a WebDAV server (Nextcloud, ownCloud, etc.). The server never sees plaintext. Pulling opens a merge view — nothing is overwritten silently.
sync.hint: With 2FA on Nextcloud, use an app password. Credentials stay in session memory only — re-enter after restart.
sync.pushToUpdate: Push to update the WebDAV copy.
sync.savedLocally: Saved locally. Push to update the WebDAV copy.

updates.title: App updates
updates.description: Checks GitHub Releases for a newer version. Nothing happens automatically — this only runs when you click the button, and nothing downloads or installs without another explicit click.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.description: Permanently delete the local vault. Cloud backups are not touched.
danger.placeholder: Type DELETE to enable the button

errorBoundary.title: Something went wrong
errorBoundary.body: SecureVault hit an unexpected error. Your vault is encrypted on disk — nothing was lost.

conflict.keepLocalDescription: Discard the remote version. Re-uploads on next sync.

createVault.hintPlaceholder: A clue — never the password itself
createVault.hintHelp: Stored locally, never synced. Must not contain your password.
createVault.notice: Zero-knowledge design: Your master password is never stored or transmitted. It derives your vault key using Argon2id (64 MiB, 3 iterations). If you forget it, your vault cannot be recovered.
createVault.doneBody: Your vault is encrypted and ready to use.

plaintextExport.body: The CSV file will contain every password, TOTP secret, and note unencrypted. Anyone with access to the file can read it. Delete it securely once you're done, and never upload it anywhere.

recoveryKit.title: Recovery Kit
recoveryKit.downloadedBody: Store the file and the passphrase separately, somewhere durable.
recoveryKit.intro: Generates a random recovery passphrase, independent of your master password, and a snapshot of your current vault that opens only with it. Use this if you ever forget your master password — there is no other way to recover a zero-knowledge vault.
recoveryKit.snapshotHint: This is a point-in-time snapshot — entries added after today won't be in it. Regenerate periodically to keep it useful.
recoveryKit.shownOnce: This passphrase is shown once and never saved anywhere. Write it down or store it in a separate password manager — not next to the downloaded file.

tagManager.empty: No tags yet — add some from an entry's edit form.

upgradeEncryption.title: Upgrade Encryption
upgradeEncryption.enterPassword: Enter your master password to confirm.
upgradeEncryption.doneBody: Your vault now uses Argon2id — the modern, memory-hard key derivation function.
upgradeEncryption.intro: This vault was created with an older key derivation function (PBKDF2-SHA256). Re-encrypt it with Argon2id — stronger against offline brute-force — using the same master password.
